object.boundary: fixed-width little-endian low bytes and separate carry bit

lenses.observation: The exact registered serial_adc_to_inclusive_gp_v1 template emits a replayable source/target/domain witness. Renamed graphs remain executable but are not accepted by this template-only rule.
limitations: Reachability of one supplied rewrite is not equivalence or a search over the 25 world policies.
The Python serial/prefix controls are not the frozen native production engine.
next_evidence: Declare a finite generator grammar, enumerate reachable forms without embedding targets, and retain witnesses and unreachable cases.

metrics.reason: No general policy generator or finite search-space denominator is implemented.

lenses.observation: The native original-add64 composition agrees with independent bigint low bytes and carry for 610 one-limb and 1024 four-limb corpus cases per collection. Both collections reuse the same corpus, not independent doubled coverage. Python serial/prefix controls separately have boundary and tiny exhaustive tests.
limitations: Finite corpus agreement is not full-domain proof or cryptographic eligibility.
Large timed dataset outputs were checked for checksum stability, not individually replayed against bigint.
next_evidence: Freeze a held-out correctness corpus before constructing new native representations; compare decoded bytes and separate carry with both original control and bigint.

lenses.observation: The retained review reports exhaustion of 131072 input triples for each of two eight-bit layouts and two supplied templates: 524288 candidate executions, not 262144 distinct triples. Ordinary tests also exhaust five smaller domains.
limitations: This bounded tiny-domain observation is not a proof for all 64-bit or 256-bit inputs.
Typed graphs can still be arithmetically incoherent; full-domain definedness does not follow merely from WORD/BIT types.
next_evidence: Supply a reviewed symbolic proof or mechanically checkable full-domain artifact binding evaluator semantics, encode/decode and the exact candidate implementation.

metrics.name: native_full_domain_equivalence
metrics.reason: No full-domain artifact covers the native 64/256-bit boundary.

lenses.observation: Model fixtures reject invalid widths/moduli, non-bit carries, malformed states, forward references and incoherent FINISH carry2. Native CLI fixtures reject malformed fields, carry values and unsupported resource requests.
limitations: Invalid-input fixtures establish selected rejection branches, not every API precondition in the engine.
The CLI parser contract is not the production pointer or modular API contract.
next_evidence: List exact preconditions of the next candidate and add one rejection fixture per branch plus a definedness argument.

metrics.name: full_precondition_discharge
metrics.reason: No complete production/candidate precondition ledger is imported.

lenses.observation: The model keeps low limbs and carry explicitly; FINISH adds its two carry contributions and rejects carry2 rather than hiding it with OR. Native boundary cases include maximal limbs and carry propagation across limb boundaries.
limitations: Observed boundary cases are not a complete machine overflow/range proof.
Neither Fp nor Fn reduction bounds follow from this modulus-free addition slice.
next_evidence: Derive node-by-node ranges for each carried state and inspect the lowered unsigned operations before introducing redundancy or delayed normalization.

metrics.name: native_range_proof
metrics.reason: No complete source-to-machine range proof is imported.

lenses.observation: Python boundary states are immutable tuples. Native bulk input/output vectors are disjoint. The conditioned native recurrence explicitly calls original_add(a,b,carry,a), so output==a is exercised by the small latency bigint smoke replay.
limitations: This narrow in-place smoke observation does not establish a general production alias matrix.
output==b, arbitrary partial overlaps and all production modular API alias contracts remain untested here.
next_evidence: Declare disjoint, exact-in-place and partial-overlap behavior at the selected real API boundary; test the supported cases and reject forbidden ones.

metrics.name: native_alias_matrix

lenses.observation: The current observable boundary includes fixed-width little-endian low bytes and a separate final carry. Native malformed-input tests also check failure status and absence of successful output.
limitations: This is a diagnostic harness boundary, not FieldElement, Scalar, group or signature API equivalence.
No hidden normalization is allowed to erase a carry mismatch.
next_evidence: When lifting the primitive into a region, include caller-visible status, carried magnitude, output bytes and mutation behavior in the differential contract.

lenses.method: static trace review plus leakage experiment
lenses.observation: The available timing and assembly artifacts are performance diagnostics, not a constant-time experiment. No secret-bearing candidate has a leakage result in this snapshot.
limitations: Stable timing averages or an add/adc sequence do not certify constant time.
The Python evaluator is not a constant-time implementation.
next_evidence: Declare secrets/public inputs, inspect branch/address traces in the exact lowered binary and perform a preregistered leakage test with explicit statistical limits.

metrics.name: constant_time_evidence
metrics.reason: Neither a complete static trace review nor a leakage experiment is imported.

lenses.observation: The runner enforces observed-memory headroom, at most 256 MiB working memory, at most one billion logical operations and one million passes. The typed model bounds regions to 128 nodes. Existing native workloads fit the declared collector ceilings.
limitations: Collector feasibility is not feasibility of all generated worlds or a production latency/memory budget.
One serial timing worker intentionally avoids concurrent benchmark interference; no multicore throughput claim follows.
next_evidence: Preregister candidate hard ceilings including conversions, table storage and complete output materialization; retain resource-failure outcomes.

lenses.observation: In the registered four-by-64 macro model, serial has region/output depth 4/4 and prefix has 5/5. Each registered multi-output operation is one atomic unit-cost DAG node. The prefix control shows no depth improvement in this bounded model.
limitations: Static macro depth is neither instruction dependency depth nor measured cycles.
The null result does not establish compiled prefix inferiority; changing operation granularity needs a declared separate model.
next_evidence: Lower candidate operations explicitly, retain both macro and lowered dependency graphs, and compare with measured latency without post-hoc favorable weights.

metrics.name: lowered_native_dependency_depth
metrics.reason: Only the typed macro model is imported; no exact instruction DAG has been extracted.

lenses.observation: The declared four-limb schedules have peak live values 11 for serial and 16 for prefix, with peak logical live bits 578 and 579. Separately, the actual native conditioned four-limb loop has stack loads/stores in the retained disassembly.
limitations: The model assumes inputs initially resident and allocates outputs before freeing last-use inputs; it is not register allocation.
Model prefix liveness is not a measurement of the native serial harness, and logical live bits are not stack footprint.
next_evidence: Bind alternative schedules and lowered code, then count actual spill loads/stores and register pressure for each compiled candidate.

metrics.name: compiled_peak_registers_and_spills
metrics.reason: The observed stack accesses have not been turned into a complete versioned liveness/spill accounting.

lenses.observation: The four-limb serial model contains 4 ADC nodes; prefix contains 4 SPLIT_GP, 3 COMPOSE_GP, 3 APPLY_GP and 4 FINISH nodes, totaling 14. The native four-limb baseline composes four original add64 calls; no compiled prefix candidate is timed.
limitations: Different macro operation types do not have equal machine cost.
More macro operations do not imply slower execution; loop overhead, locality and lowering remain separate evidence.
next_evidence: Retain typed operation vectors and actual compiler instruction classes alongside complete-region measurements, without collapsing them into an invented unit-cost score.

metrics.name: candidate_native_operation_multiset
metrics.reason: No lowered new-method candidate is imported.

lenses.observation: The model separately counts input decomposition as 2*limbs divmod operations and output construction as limbs shifts, limbs sum terms and one fixed-width serialization. Native timing excludes allocation, initialization and final checksum.
limitations: These are static counts of an explicit Python boundary algorithm, not conversion timings.
Baseline arithmetic timing excludes work that a non-identity representation may require at region boundaries.
next_evidence: Preregister encode/decode/normalization boundaries and measure both isolated conversion and complete-region cost, retaining amortization assumptions.

metrics.name: native_conversion_cost
metrics.reason: No non-identity native representation conversion has been implemented or timed.

lenses.observation: Both archived collections contain warmed repeated one-limb and four-limb conditioned recurrences. The numbers are nanoseconds per complete logical addition, including rotate/XOR input conditioning and loop/spill overhead.
limitations: This is not isolated ADC latency or a prefix/carry-save result.
CPU0 exhibited synchronized nonstationarity; CPU4 was selected after observing it. Collections remain separate and all outliers remain retained.
next_evidence: Measure original control and each candidate interleaved in the same fresh session, with identical recurrence and boundary; report uncertainty without comparing against a historical best.

lenses.observation: The same native bulk arithmetic has small-hot and LLC-exceeding working-set measurements for both widths. On CPU4 the four-limb median is approximately 3.005 ns hot and 6.536 ns large, with complete input/output records materialized.
limitations: These are baseline regime observations, not a new-method gain, causal locality proof or DRAM bandwidth measurement.
The CPU4 large four-limb maximum near 7.965 ns remains in its seven samples; no pooling with CPU0 or PMU repeats.
next_evidence: Hold method fixed while varying layout/capacity, and hold layout/capacity fixed while varying method; retain complete boundaries and same-session controls.

lenses.observation: Separate CPU4 perf stat -r 3 diagnostics retain user-space cpu_core instruction event aggregate counts and variation for the hot and large four-limb benchmark processes.
limitations: Counters include initialization, internal warmup, checksum and runtime work outside the C++ timed loop.
Per-repetition PMU counts are not exported; raw process counts divided by timed additions are not exact arithmetic CPI or isolated kernel instructions.
The separate PMU artifact records event names and the measured binary identity, but not the perf executable version; a new collection must add it.
next_evidence: Introduce an explicitly scoped region-only PMU measurement with a validated boundary and overhead control before attributing instruction counts to candidate arithmetic.

lenses.observation: The separate whole-process diagnostics retain generic cpu_core cache-reference and cache-miss event counts. Logical bulk record sizes are 40 and 112 bytes; large-record accounting gives about 17.1 logical GB/s, not observed memory-controller traffic.
limitations: Generic cache events are not DRAM bytes; initialization, warmup and checksum contribute.
The compiler may read only a byte of the carry slot, while cache fills, write allocation and spills introduce other traffic; process counters do not isolate the cause of elapsed-time differences.
The separate PMU artifact records event names and the measured binary identity, but not the perf executable version; a new collection must add it.
next_evidence: Collect region-scoped cache events and platform-supported memory-controller traffic with an explicit causal layout/working-set experiment.
